pairs.reason: Same claim reordered; 'humanity' for 'human beings' changes nothing a respondent would act on.
Only spells out 'be received' as 'how people will receive it'; scope and claim unchanged.
Dropping 'remain' removes a mild presupposition that authority already rests on self-government, but agree/disagree sets stay the same.

'Greatly exaggerated' sets a higher bar than 'inflated', and 'what AI will achieve' narrows scope to capability promises (leaving out safety or benefit-sharing promises), so someone who sees the promises as moderately inflated could agree with the original and disagree with the rewrite; dropping 'hype' also softens the implied motive.
pairs.fix: Most public promises about advanced AI are exaggerated hype.

new.problems: 'Fear' frames concern as emotional, not reasoned; it does not say fear of which harms (job loss, misuse, extinction) or which evidence; different camps will read it as being about different risks.
new.rewrite: Public concern about the risks of AI is greater than the current evidence justifies.

new.problems: 'Serious' and 'well before' make it sound like common prudence, so it is close to obvious; the real disagreement (control work done in advance versus alongside deployment) is hidden. 'Such systems' is also vague.
new.rewrite: Most work on controlling advanced AI should be done before such systems are built, rather than alongside their development.
